full_judgment:
6. Since the defendants, in their written statement, supported the plaintiffs case to the effect that they had no objection if the suit was decreed and did not contest the suit, the trial judge proceeded for ex-parte disposal and after conclusion of ex-parte hearing, learned Joint District Judge dismissed the suit by the impugned judgment and decree mainly on the ground of limitation. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the same, the plaintiffs preferred the instant first appeal. 

 9. Mr Rahman further submits that the time-frame given in the contract must be read with the conditions No.1 and 3 as incorporated there. In view of the failure of reciprocal promise by the vendor, the plaintiffs were well within the limitation. The one year time-frame as mentioned in the contract was not of the essence of contract. Learned trial judge dismissed the suit on the ground of limitation on total misconception of law. In support of his submission Mr Rahman refers to the cases of Abdus Sobhan (Md) vs Md Ahsanullah and others 21 BLC (AD) 268 and Amir Hossain Sowdagar vs Md Harunur Rashid and others 65 DLR (AD) 130. 

 10. We have considered the submissions of the learned advocates and gone through the records. Admittedly there was an agreement between the parties for sale of the suit property for a consideration of Taka 15,00,000, out of which Taka 14,00,000 was readily paid. It was stipulated that the vendor would collect the sale permission from RAJUK within 6 months from the date of execution and registration of the agreement. It was further stipulated that after obtaining the sale permission, the vendor would execute and register the sale-deed within the next twelve months receiving the remaining consideration. When the proposed vendor Aziza Begum died leaving behind the defendants as her legal heirs and successors, it was their responsibility to perform their part of the contract. Despite making request and service of notices (vide Exhibits 11 series) the defendants failed to do that and in that event the plaintiffs instituted the suit for specific performance of contract. From a careful reading of the terms of agreement if appears that the time-frame of institution of the suit is co-related with the reciprocal promise of obtaining the sale permission from RAJUK on the part of the vendor Aziza Begum, since deceased. So long the vendor/her heirs and successors would not obtain permission from RAJUK question of registration of sale deed on payment of the remaining consideration would not arise. Similarly, so long they would not deny to file application for sale permission, or to obtain the sale permission, or to register the sale-deed, question of institution of the suit would not arise. After the death of Aziza Begum, when the plaintiffs made request and served legal notice upon her legal heirs and successors (defendants herein) and despite receipt of the same, they did not response, the cause of action for institution of the suit arose. It has already been stated that the agreement for sale was registered on 11-2-2013, the vendor Aziza Begum died on 26-6-2014, plaintiffs requested the heirs of Aziza Begurn. (defendants herein) on 12-12-2014 to apply for the sale permission, and served legal notice upon them on 23-12-2014 and again on 5-1-2015. Getting no response, they instituted the suit on 21-5-2015, which was well within the time. According to Article 113 to the First Schedule of the Limitation Act limitation for institution of a suit for specific performance of contract is one year to be computed from the date fixed for performance or when the plaintiffs have notice that performance is refused. The law of limitation, time-frame stipulated in the present contract must be read with conditions No.1 and 3 thereof, which provide a reciprocal promise on the part of the promisee, and, as such, the limitation in the present case would be computed from implied refusal of the defendants. 

 13. In the present case, no default clause was there in the sale agreement as to what would happen if the vendor failed to obtain or did not obtain the sale permission within the stipulated time and thereby did not perform her part of the contract. So, there is no scope, to say that the present suit was barred by limitation. The finding of the learned Joint District Judge regarding limitation was, therefore, not correct.
